signals.statement: The PCS controller publishes the battery's state of charge every fifteen minutes, sampled after that instant's events. One sample in fifty does not arrive.
The PCS controller publishes the mean AC power over the span that just ended: positive while discharging to the bus, negative while charging from it.
The PV inverter publishes the mean AC power it delivered over the span that just ended - what was used, not what the array could have offered.
The residential feeder meter publishes the mean power served to the feeder over the span that just ended.
The clinic meter publishes the mean power served to the clinic over the span that just ended.
The mill meter publishes the mean power served to the mill over the span that just ended.

generator.reported_status: Reported generator status is pending T025b, and staging it is T026's. The state shown here is the simulator's private physical state, not a reading any device reported.

discrete_state_rules.display_name: Discrete transitions happen at step boundaries only
discrete_state_rules.statement: At T, a lifecycle deadline already due (a start delay that has elapsed) is applied first, before the sample at T. The controller then reads its local view and emits intent; a transition that request causes is applied at T after the sample, never treated as already due before its own observation. Every transition records the state address, previous and next values, the cause and controller reference, and the instant. Start delay, minimum runtime and generator policy windows must be whole multiples of the step or setup refuses them; minimum runtime counts from the boundary the state became RUNNING.

discrete_state_rules.display_name: The Site's frozen policy owns generator control
discrete_state_rules.statement: The generator is requested to start only when the state of charge at T is at or below the Site's start threshold, and to stop only when it is RUNNING, the Site's minimum runtime has elapsed and the state of charge is at or above the stop threshold. The model adds no trigger of its own. Sources serve load in the Site's frozen source priority; a running generator serves what the sources ahead of it do not and may charge the battery only when the battery is not discharging, within the PCS limit and headroom. The rating is a ceiling, fuel is checked before energy is accepted, and fuel falls by the specific consumption times accepted generator energy, with no idle or start fuel.

discrete_state_rules.display_name: A request, a physical state and an output are three things
discrete_state_rules.statement: A run request is not RUNNING, and RUNNING is not output: a generator that is STARTING delivers nothing, and FAILED is inert and delivers nothing without failing the execution. A physical state is neither a switch position nor a controller mode, and it is not a reported reading until a publication profile publishes it.

coupling_rules.display_name: The controller reads a local view at T
coupling_rules.statement: The controller's view at T is built from its declared local inputs after T's events: the state of charge, the reserve in effect, the irradiance and each load's demand in effect at T. It is never a published reading and is not derived from one, so a reporting cadence, a dropout or a gap changes no controller decision. The view is an immutable record; nothing the controller does can change the world.

coupling_rules.display_name: Intent and acceptance are two records
coupling_rules.statement: The controller emits requests for [T, T+dt) - for example a battery discharge of 30 kW. The resolver accepts what the installation allows - 22 kW through a 22 kW PCS - and records why. Both numbers are kept. Only accepted flows move a stock or reach a later reading; a request never does.

coupling_rules.display_name: The resolver is a declared cascade
coupling_rules.statement: PV potential is rated power times irradiance over 1000 W/m2, capped by the inverter. Sources serve load in the Site's source priority, and loads are served in its critical-load priority: a load is served in full before the next one gets anything. The battery discharges no faster than the PCS limit and the request allow and not below the reserve in effect; it charges from PV surplus no faster than the PCS limit and the request allow and not above full. PV nobody can use is curtailed. There is no iterative solver and no tolerance.

coupling_rules.display_name: A step is evaluated in segments where inputs change
coupling_rules.statement: Where a forcing's window starts or ends inside a step, the resolver evaluates that step as consecutive segments split at those instants, each with the values in effect across it, and the state of charge carried from one segment to the next. No value is applied early, stretched across the step or averaged.

Every step's accepted flows satisfy their balances exactly in rational arithmetic: PV potential equals PV to load, PV to battery, curtailment and inverter clipping; energy taken into the battery equals energy stored plus charging loss; energy taken out equals energy delivered plus discharging loss; demand equals service plus unserved load, for each load and in total; and the stored-energy change equals what was stored less what was taken out. A balance that does not hold fails the run as BALANCE_IDENTITY_VIOLATION. Nothing is absorbed by a tolerance.
